wordOrder.title: Put the words in order

matching.title: Match the -ing form

timedMC.title: Beat the clock
timedMC.subtitle: 15 seconds per question. Some of these need the past continuous — but watch for stative verbs, and the short action that interrupts a longer one.

errorCorrection.title: Find the mistake
errorCorrection.subtitle: Each sentence has exactly one mistake. Tap the word you think is wrong. Twenty original sentences.

items.message: With 'you', use 'were', not 'was'.
With 'they', use 'were', not 'was'.
A background action in progress needs was/were + -ing — 'was walking', not just 'walking'.
The background action needs was/were + -ing — 'was cooking', not just 'cooking'.
The past continuous needs was/were before the -ing form — 'was doing', not just 'doing'.
The short interrupting action takes the past simple, not the continuous — 'started', not 'was starting'.
The longer background action takes the past continuous — 'was having', not 'had'.
State verbs like 'know' never take the continuous — use the past simple, 'knew'.
State verbs like 'know' stay in the past simple, even in the negative.
Double the final consonant — 'swimming', not 'swiming'.
Drop the silent 'e' before adding -ing — 'writing', not 'writeing'.
Change 'ie' to 'y' before adding -ing — 'lying', not 'liing'.
With 'you', use 'were', not 'was'.
With 'she', use 'was', not 'were'.
The negative past continuous needs wasn't/weren't — 'wasn't checking', not 'not checking'.
With 'he', use 'was', not 'were'.
The short interrupting action takes the past simple — 'rang', not the -ing form alone.
The background action needs was/were + -ing — 'were eating', not just 'eating'.
With 'we', use 'were', not 'was'.
State verbs like 'want' never take the continuous — use the past simple, 'wanted'.
